sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What are we doing when we sketch an object to show it is 'on the move'?
options: A) Drawing stiff, straight lines
B) Capturing frozen shapes
C) Using action lines or tilted angles to show speed
D) Erasing the entire sketch
questions.answer: C) Using action lines or tilted angles to show speed

questions.question_text: Which technique is most helpful when planning the sequence of events for 'Picturing Stories'?
options: A) Mixing all colors blindly
B) Drawing a storyboard with ordered panels
C) Using only black and white paint
D) Tearing the paper into tiny pieces
questions.answer: B) Drawing a storyboard with ordered panels

questions.question_text: In the lesson 'Peeping Out of the Window', what purpose does the window frame serve in your drawing?
options: A) It acts as a border to focus on a specific view
B) It covers the entire artwork
C) It makes the drawing look like a circle
D) It hides the background completely
questions.answer: A) It acts as a border to focus on a specific view

questions.question_text: When creating an 'Imaginary Being', what is the best way to develop your creature?
options: A) Copying exactly what you see in a photograph
B) Combining parts of different real animals together
C) Tracing a perfect square
D) Drawing a plain, empty box
questions.answer: B) Combining parts of different real animals together

questions.question_text: What is the most important element when making a poster for 'Spreading the Message'?
options: A) Very small, hidden text
B) Dull, matching colors
C) Bold text and an eye-catching illustration
D) Leaving most of the paper blank
questions.answer: C) Bold text and an eye-catching illustration

questions.question_text: Which materials are primarily used in the 'Stitch it for a Story' art form?
options: A) Clay and water
B) Needle, thread, and fabric
C) Wood and nails
D) Crayons and glass

questions.question_text: To 'Create a Scene' that looks realistic, how should objects in the far background appear?
options: A) Larger than objects in the front
B) Exactly the same size as objects in the front
C) Smaller and less detailed than objects in the front
D) Brighter and bolder than everything else
questions.answer: C) Smaller and less detailed than objects in the front

questions.question_text: What does the 'Time Team Technique' usually require artists to do?
options: A) Work entirely alone without talking
B) Collaborate and divide tasks among a group
C) Finish a drawing in two seconds
D) Paint with their eyes closed
questions.answer: B) Collaborate and divide tasks among a group

questions.question_text: When we 'View and Review' a classmate's artwork, what should we provide?
options: A) Constructive feedback and positive observations
B) Only negative comments
C) Absolute silence
D) Instructions to throw it away
questions.answer: A) Constructive feedback and positive observations

questions.question_text: Which of these is a way to add physical texture to a flat paper drawing?
options: A) Erasing the pencil marks gently
B) Drawing very straight lines
C) Gluing sand, yarn, or crumpled tissue onto it
D) Looking at it from a distance
questions.answer: C) Gluing sand, yarn, or crumpled tissue onto it

questions.question_text: How can you show that a strong wind is blowing in a drawing of a tree? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To show wind blowing in a drawing, you can draw slanted lines, bending tree branches, and leaves or hair swirling in the same direction.

questions.question_text: Name three materials you can use in 'Stitch it for a Story' and explain why they are useful. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: You can use colorful threads, small beads, and scrap fabric pieces. Stitching these materials together adds 3D texture and makes the story visually interesting.

questions.question_text: Why is using a window frame perspective helpful when sketching an outdoor landscape? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Using a window frame as a border helps focus the viewer's eye on specific details outside, acting like a natural camera lens to capture a specific view.

questions.question_text: What is a storyboard, and how does it help an artist picture a story? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A storyboard is a series of square panels showing illustrations in order. It helps artists plan the beginning, middle, and end of their visual story clearly.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to 'View and Review' your own artwork after completing it? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Reviewing helps an artist understand what looks good and what needs improvement. Constructive feedback allows them to grow, learn new techniques, and create better future artworks.

questions.question_text: Design an 'Imaginary Being' by combining features of two different animals. Describe its appearance, colors, and special abilities. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: My imaginary being is a 'Dragon-Flyer'. It has the large, scaly green body of a dragon, but the delicate, shimmering transparent wings of a butterfly. It breathes colorful bubbles instead of fire, and its long tail ends in a glowing yellow lantern.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are asked to 'Create a Scene' of a busy morning market. Describe the objects you would place in the foreground and background. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would draw a busy morning market scene. In the foreground, vendors are selling bright red tomatoes and yellow bananas from wooden carts. In the background, people are carrying cloth bags, while a sleeping dog rests under a shaded canopy.

questions.question_text: Describe the step-by-step process of designing a poster aimed at 'Spreading the Message' about saving water in your school. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: To make an effective poster about saving water, I would first sketch a large, eye-catching image of a single blue water drop holding the earth. I would use bold, block letters for the slogan 'Save Water, Save Life' at the top, and use bright, contrasting colors to grab immediate attention.

questions.question_text: Explain how you would use the 'Time Team Technique' with three classmates to paint a large mural of a forest. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For a 'Time Team' project, my group would assign specific roles. One person would sketch the characters, another would color the backgrounds, and a third would arrange them. By dividing the tasks, we can work simultaneously and combine our different artistic strengths to finish the large mural efficiently and creatively.
